title: Machine-learned density functional theory reveals molecular control of electrolyte screening
summary: Machine-learned neural classical density functional theory trained on grand-canonical Monte Carlo data enabled calculations of asymptotic screening behavior across increasingly molecularly detailed electrolyte models. The authors report that solvent attraction creates a monotonic decay mode, solvent polarity produces re-entrant behavior, and ionic architecture changes screening-length exponents, challenging a single universal scaling law. These are computational predictions for modelled systems; the reviewed paper reports no experimental validation of the new predictions.
organization: University of Cambridge; Durham University; Stanford University

evidence.tested: Computed decay lengths across primitive and molecular electrolyte models; neural cDFT approach compared against known primitive-model behavior.
evidence.unknown: No experimental validation of the new molecular-structure predictions is reported in the reviewed paper.
evidence.ai_role: Neural cDFT trained on grand-canonical Monte Carlo samples supplies direct correlation functions and enables efficient screening-pole analysis across electrolyte models.

source_review.scope: Full arXiv v1 HTML Results, Conclusions and Methods; official abstract page and submission history.
